title: Customs Duty Exemption Policy and Regulatory Adjustments
summary: This thread tracks the evolution of customs duty exemptions granted under Section 19 of the Customs Act, 1969. It reflects a shift from broad, static exemptions to dynamic, sector-specific adjustments (e.g., medical equipment, pre-fabricated buildings) and the integration of VAT/Supplementary Duty laws into the exemption framework.

evolution.legal_basis: Transitioned from Customs Act 1969 to Customs Act 2023, increasingly integrated with VAT & Supplementary Duty Act 2012.
evolution.scope: Moved from general exemptions to targeted industrial and medical sector support.
evolution.structure: Shifted from simple duty waivers to complex HS Code-based conditional exemptions.

timeline.change: Established exemption from pre-shipment inspection for specific duty-exempt goods.
HS Code substitution for specific exempted goods.
Reduction of duty rates for specific exempted categories from 3% to 2%.
Shift to alignment with the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012 for exemption administration.
Transition to the Customs Act, 2023 framework for local industrial exemptions.

Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: This act provides the enabling power to grant exemptions from value added tax and supplementary duty for specified medical equipment imports.
Hospitals benefiting from these exemptions must comply with the registration, filing, and procedural requirements stipulated in this act.
National Board of Revenue: The board acts as the central authority for issuing these exemptions in the public interest and is responsible for making decisions regarding time extensions for the installation of imported medical equipment.
The board establishes and supervises the committee responsible for physical inspection and verification of the installed equipment.
Industrial IRC Holder: To qualify for duty and tax exemptions, the importing hospital must hold a valid Industrial IRC as an industrial consumer issued by the relevant regulatory authority.
Customs Duty: A specific exemption is provided for customs duty on medical equipment imports, covering the amount exceeding the first one percent of the value-based duty rate.
This exemption applies subject to strict conditions, including mandatory post-import installation and usage verification.
Regulatory Duty: Total exemption is granted from all regulatory duties for the medical equipment listed in the table provided in this order.
Value Added Tax: Total exemption from all value added taxes is granted to qualifying hospitals importing the specified medical equipment, provided all procedural and compliance conditions are met.
Supplementary Duty: Total exemption from all supplementary duties is granted for the medical equipment listed in this order, subject to the fulfillment of prescribed usage and installation conditions.
Advance Tax: Imported medical equipment listed in the table is exempted from all advance tax payments, provided the importing hospital maintains compliance with all regulatory conditions.
Hospital: The term refers to multi-disciplinary or mono-disciplinary medical facilities that meet specific criteria, including a minimum bed capacity and free service provisions for the poor.
Hospitals must adhere to strict installation deadlines for imported equipment and are subject to mandatory system-based audits every three years to retain their concessionary status.
Indemnity Bond: Importing hospitals must execute and submit an indemnity bond on non-judicial stamp paper to the customs authority, covering the amount of exempted duties and taxes, which remains subject to return upon successful verification of equipment installation.
System Based Audit: Hospitals utilizing these concessionary benefits are mandatorily required to undergo a system-based audit every three years to ensure continued compliance with customs regulations.
